key_insight: Adding 1 wt.% CeO₂ or La₂O₃ to HVOF-sprayed WC–12Co refined grains, reduced porosity, and increased microhardness by 6% and 4%, respectively.
engineering_relevance: Rare-earth oxide reinforcement offers a route to denser, more wear-resistant WC–12Co coatings without compromising bond strength.
method: Deposit unreinforced and CeO₂- or La₂O₃-reinforced WC–12Co coatings using HVOF.
Compare microstructure, phase composition, bond strength, microhardness, abrasive wear, and friction.
Examine worn surfaces by SEM to identify wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: WC–12Co–1La₂O₃ achieved the minimum reported wear rate of 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), while WC–12Co–1CeO₂ achieved the lowest friction coefficient of 0.4; reinforcement did not affect bond strength relative to the unreinforced value of 73.60 ± 5 MPa.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or long-term durability, limiting direct transfer of these results to service environments.
paper_title: EFFECT OF CEO2 AND LA2O3 REINFORCEMENTS ON MECHANICAL, TRIBOLOGICAL AND MICROSTRUCTURAL PROPERTIES OF WC–12CO COATING BY HIGH-VELOCITY OXYGEN FUEL DEPOSITION TECHNIQUE
